top_categories.workout_context: 170 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.

Road-specific control matters at Chasing Cancellara Bern to Zermatt. Practice on point-to-point Alpine road ultra: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 170 miles.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 170 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Chasing Cancellara Bern to Zermatt's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before race day.
When someone attacks on point-to-point Alpine road ultra, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
170 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.

Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Chasing Cancellara Bern to Zermatt. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Chasing Cancellara Bern to Zermatt's point-to-point Alpine road ultra rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
At Chasing Cancellara Bern to Zermatt, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what Chasing Cancellara Bern to Zermatt's point-to-point Alpine road ultra actually does to you.
2-minute all-out efforts on point-to-point Alpine road ultra. Closing gaps, responding to attacks, sprinting for position. Train the burn.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Chasing Cancellara Bern to Zermatt. Train it until it feels boring.

race_overlay.heat: A dark start, long valley exposure, and a high-mountain finish create cold, heat, wind, rain, and fast weather-change risk across one enormous day. Begin heat acclimatization 10–14 days before Chasing Cancellara Bern to Zermatt — 20–30min sauna sessions or midday rides in full kit. Pre-load sodium 48 hours out. Target 500–750ml/hr with electrolytes on race day. Race-day realities: Valley heat before mountain cold.
race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 170 miles: 80–100g carbs/hour from mile 1 — don’t wait until you’re hungry. Practice your exact race-day nutrition in every long training ride. Carry backup calories. 170 miles burns 8,000–12,000+ calories — you cannot replace them all, but you must try.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Chasing Cancellara Bern to Zermatt. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The technical descents at Chasing Cancellara Bern to Zermatt demand practice on similar paved roads. Ride point-to-point alpine road ultra at race-day cadence weekly. Practice braking points, corner entry, line choice, and accelerating smoothly out of turns. Confirm tire pressure and equipment before race week.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Road Specific, and Endurance to prepare you for 170 miles of point-to-point alpine road ultra in Ittigen near Bern to Zermatt, Switzerland.
